Annotated walkthrough

Solid marks point at the element a finding is about. Dashed marks show related context. Positions come from the page's DOM, not from reading the image.

1Finding 1

A new issue has no assignee by default, so it is missing from My issues, which opens on Assigned

Slows or risks the taskConfidence high

No matching issuesstep 6, zoomed

My issues: Assignedfull screen

Observed
In the Create issue dialog the assignee button reads "Assignee", described as "Currently no one is assigned" (step 4). The issue was saved with that default as MYA-5. My issues opens on the Assigned tab, which reads "No matching issues" and "2 issues hidden by display options" (step 6). MYA-5 is listed only under the Created tab (step 8). The Assigned empty state does not mention MYA-5 or the Created tab.
Why it matters
Finding the issue again is the second half of the task. The product's own name for the list, My issues, and its default tab both lead away from the issue the user just made, and the empty state blames display options instead of the missing assignee.
Hypothesis
New users decide the issue was not saved, or create it again. Not observed with real users.
Recommendation
When Assigned is empty and the user created unassigned issues, say so in the empty state: "You created MYA-5. It isn't assigned to anyone." with Assign to me and View created. A reasonable designer could prefer making the creator the default assignee in a workspace with one member; that changes team behaviour, so test it before shipping.
Evidence
Dialog defaults and list contents read from the DOM at steps 4, 6 and 8. One automated run.
2Finding 2

The empty state says issues are hidden by display options but not which option or which issues

Minor frictionConfidence medium

Completed issues: Past daystep 7, zoomed

Display optionsfull screen

Observed
The Assigned tab reads "2 issues hidden by display options" with a Show options button (step 6). The button opens a panel with grouping, sub-grouping, ordering, completed issues set to "Past day", sub-issue settings and eleven display properties (step 7). No setting is marked as the one hiding the issues. The Inbox lists two onboarding issues, MYA-4 and MYA-2, both Canceled and closed by Linear (step 9).
Why it matters
The note explains the empty list with a cause the user did not set and cannot find. It also pulls attention to filters at the moment the real cause is the missing assignee in finding 1.
Hypothesis
The two hidden issues are the canceled onboarding issues, hidden by the completed-issues window. Inferred from the inbox, not confirmed in the list.
Recommendation
Name the cause in the note, for example "2 canceled issues hidden. Show", and let one click reveal them without opening the panel.
Evidence
Note text and panel settings read from the DOM at steps 6 and 7; inbox rows at step 9.
3Finding 3

The workspace opens on an agent chat, and issue creation is an unlabelled 28 px icon

ObservationConfidence medium

Create new issue iconstep 3, zoomed

First screen in the new workspacefull screen

Observed
After sign-in the workspace opens on "New chat" with "Introducing Linear Agent", a message box "Ask Linear…" and a notice "Linear Agent is now your default view" with Change and Keep (step 3). The only visible way to create an issue is a 28 × 28 px icon with no text label next to the workspace name. Clicking it opened the Create issue dialog (step 4).
Why it matters
This did not block the task: one click on the icon worked. It is noted because the first screen promotes asking the agent over creating an issue directly, and a user who wants to make an issue has to recognise the icon.
Hypothesis
Some new users type the issue into the agent chat instead. Not observed.
Recommendation
No change needed for this task. If the agent view stays the default for new workspaces, consider a labelled New issue entry on that screen.
Evidence
Icon size read from the DOM at step 3.

How findings are ranked

Blocks the task
The task cannot be finished on the tested path, or only by a route most users would not find.
Slows or risks the task
The task can be finished, but the issue costs real effort, causes errors, or puts the user's work at risk within the flow.
Minor friction
The task is finished with some extra effort or searching. Recovery is easy.
Observation
Worth knowing, not friction in this flow. Consequence is noted separately when it could be high.

What this audit cannot see

  • Human time

    How long the task takes a person. Times recorded here are machine times and are not reported.

  • Real user behaviour

    Whether new users look in My issues, Inbox or search first, and whether they assign themselves.

  • Signup and workspace setup

    The user signed up and named the workspace before the walk, and the workspace already held onboarding issues from months earlier. A first-day workspace may open on a different screen.

  • Settings

    Whether an account or team setting changes the default assignee. Settings pages were not opened.
